Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Cross-Coupling of Propargylic Acetates
with Chloro(vinyl)silanes: Access to Silylallenes
Chong-Hui Xu, Zhi-Qiang Xiong, Jing-Hao Qin,* Xin-Hua Xu, and Jin-Heng Li*
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2024, 89, 2885−2894

ABSTRACT: Because of their various reactivities, propargyl
acetates are refined chemical intermediates that are extensively
applied in pharmaceutical synthesis. Currently, reactions between
propargyl acetates and chlorosilanes may be the most effective
method for synthesizing silylallenes. Nevertheless, owing to the
adaptability and selectivity of substrates, transition metal catalysis is
difficult to achieve. Herein, nickel-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling reactions between propargyl acetates and substituted vinyl
chlorosilanes for the synthesis of tetrasubstituted silylallenes are described. Therein, metallic zinc is a crucial reductant that
effectively enables two electrophilic reagents to selectively construct C(sp
2
)−Si bonds. Additionally, a Ni-catalyzed reductive
mechanism involving a radical process is proposed on the basis of deuteration-labeled experiments.
■
INTRODUCTION
Organosilanes, such as silylallenes, are one of the most
important functional structural units in fine chemicals,
pharmaceuticals, and materials and generally emerged as
versatile synthetic intermediates in chemical synthesis.
1
Accordingly, the development of efficient synthetic method-
ologies to access these functionalized organosilanes has drawn
much ongoing interest. Among them, transition-metal-
catalyzed C−Si bond construction reactions play an important
role in such silyl compound preparation by incorporation of
the silyl functionalities and have been well investigated in
recent years.
1,2
Despite extensively documented methods for
the C−Si bond formation,
2
reports of handling the transition-
metal-catalyzed silylation of alkynes via the C(sp
2
)−Si bond
construction to access silylallenes remain rare.
3,4
Pioneering
work on transition-metal-catalyzed hydrosilylation of 1,3-
diynes with trichlorosilane to prepare trichlorosilyl allenes
has been reported by Hiyama and co-workers.
3
However, the
method suffers from both a narrow scope of 1,3-diynes and
limited resulting silylallenes. In 2001, Hayashi and co-workers
extended a similar hydrosilylation strategy to realize the first
palladium-catalyzed asymmetric hydrosilylation of 4-substi-
tuted 1-buten-3-ynes with HSiCl
3
for the synthesis of
silylallenes (Scheme 1A(a)).
4a
However, only few available
examples were examined. Subsequently, Loh, Xu and co-
workers have reported a new efficient strategy for assembling
silylallenes in particularly good yields that had high enantio-
and regioselectivity based on the copper-catalyzed 1,6-silyl
addition to enynoates with relatively expensive Si−B reagents
(Scheme 1A(b)).
4b
Cui, Li and co-workers have employed the
rare-element complexes for the effective catalytic 1,4-hydro-
silylation of 1,3-enynes with hydrosilanes to construct
tetrasubstituted silylallenes (Scheme 1A(c)), which used a
wide range of 1,3-enyne substrates to greatly broaden the
resulting silylallenes.
4c
Very recently, Rueping, Yue and co-
workers have developed a new radical strategy to realize nickel-
catalyzed three-component electroreductive cross-coupling for
the 1,4-silylalkylation of 1,3-enynes via the activation of alkyl
bromides to form the alkyl radicals, wherein chlorosilanes serve
as the electrophiles to terminate the reaction (Scheme
1A(d)).
4d
This strategy employed two electrophiles, alkyl
bromides and chlorosilanes, to initiate and terminate the
reductive cross-coupling, respectively, for accessing silylallenes.
Alternatively, decarboxylative silylation of alkyne-function-
alized cyclic carbonate derivatives using Cu
4e
or Ni catalysis
4f
for producing various silyl-substituted 2,3- and 3,4-allenols has
been developed (Scheme 1A(e)). In contrast, simple, readily
accessible propargyl acetates that contain both highly reactive
alkyne and acetate moieties can be easily converted into
functionalized allenes; however, transition-metal-catalyzed C−
Si bond formation for transformations of propargyl acetates to
silylallenes remains a formidable challenge due to propargyl
acetates having C1 and C3 reactive sites.
5
To address the
challenge, we have established an electroreductive cross-
coupling method for rendering transformations of prop-2-yn-
1-yl acetates with chloro(vinyl)silanes to form tetrasubstituted
silylallenes, wherein cathodic reduction of a chlorosilane
generates the chlorosilane radical anion and then afford the
silyl radical by cleavage of the Si−Cl bond with Mg
2+
and thus
trigger the reductive cross-coupling of prop-2-yn-1-yl acetates

CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed a novel nickel-catalyzed
reductive cross-coupling reaction of propargyl acetates with
chloro(vinyl)silanes, enabling the formation of C(sp
2
)−Si
bonds to access highly valuable tetrasubstituted silylallenes.
The reaction is highlighted by its mild reaction conditions,
broad scope of propargyl acetates, good tolerance of functional
groups, and excellent selectivity. Most importantly, this
reaction can be applicable to late-stage modification of highly
valuable natural products and pharmaceuticals.
